description: Helps you decide whether to scale paid now: it takes your customer list (signing date, segment, monthly fee and any stop or return dates) and your churn reasons, and returns, for each customer group, scale, run a capped test, or hold, with the counts behind it, the stop rule, payback, a first draft response to each churn reason and a churn interview guide. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of pmf_scorecard when you need a paid-growth decision grounded in customer cohorts and unit economics.

as_of.description: The date the list was pulled (YYYY-MM-DD). Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

billing_term.description: How customers are billed. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "monthly".

blended_cac.description: Optional: blended CAC, shown for contrast only. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

business_model.description: Business model, passed on to retention_playbook. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas_subscription".

churn_reasons.description: Reasons in customers' words, comma or line separated. Format is text. For example, "implementation delays and unclear ownership".

customers.description: One row per customer (1 to 2000 items). Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"id":"account-001","signed":"2026-11-17","segment":"manufacturers with 200 to 500 employees","monthly_fee":24000}].

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"id":"account-001","signed":"2026-11-17","segment":"manufacturers with 200 to 500 employees","monthly_fee":24000}.

id.description: An ID, never a name. Format is text. For example, "account-001".

monthly_fee.description: Monthly fee at signing (annual contracts: the yearly fee divided by 12). Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

monthly_starts.description: Optional: activity in each of the 12 months before as_of (or before stopped), for the seasonal tag. Format is a JSON array. For example, [12,11,14,13,12,15,14,13,12,14,15,13].

items.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

resumed.description: Optional: date they paid again, if they came back (YYYY-MM-DD). Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

segment.description: Segment label. Format is text. For example, "manufacturers with 200 to 500 employees".

signed.description: Signing date (YYYY-MM-DD). Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

stopped.description: Optional: the first date a payment was due and not paid (for annual contracts, the renewal date they did not renew), YYYY-MM-DD. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

gross_margin.description: Optional (0 to 1): gross margin needed for the money section. Format is a JSON number. For example, 0.8.

interview_persona.description: Role to interview, for the interview kit. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

metrics.description: Optional: each metric with its name, value, whether it counts customers or revenue, and its period. Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","value":12}].

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","value":12}.

counts.description: Optional: whether the metric counts customers or revenue. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "customers".

name.description: Metric name. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

period.description: Optional: period over which the metric is measured. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "month".

value.description: Metric value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

paid_cac.description: Optional: paid-only CAC. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

payback_line_months.description: Optional (default 12): the longest acceptable paid payback in months. 12 is Shashwat's example line for a $36,000 contract, not a benchmark. Format is a JSON number.

product.description: Product in one line. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

stop_line.description: Optional (default 0.80): share of a cohort that must still pay at month 12. 0.80 is Shashwat's example line for a $36,000 contract, not a benchmark. Format is a JSON number.

test_cap.description: Optional: all-in budget for a capped test. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

win_rate_floor.description: Optional (0 to 1): a win rate the buyer is confident paid can reach. Format is a JSON number. For example, 0.8.

win_rate_target.description: Optional (0 to 1): the highest win rate the buyer would believe. Format is a JSON number. For example, 0.8.
